title: Open Homomorphisms of Global Solvably Closed Galois Groups
main_claim: Uchida's conjecture: every continuous open homomorphism Gal(E1/F1)→Gal(E2/F2) between Galois groups of solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields is induced by a unique equivariant field embedding E2↪E1. The proof reduces to showing that every open map G_F→P=Gal(Q^s/Q) is conjugate to restriction, and then applies Hoshi's cyclotomic criterion.

issues.location: preliminaries.tex, Theorem 'Uchida's partial local correspondence' and Theorem 'Hoshi'
issues.description: Two key anabelian inputs are used as black boxes and I did not check them against the sources. The first is Uchida 1981's trichotomy plus Proposition 1, including the claims that open image (not surjectivity) is enough, that the target prime is unique, and that the target coverage is cofinite for fixed ℓ. The second is Hoshi 2025 Theorem 3.4. The paper only sketches why its stated version follows from Uchida's case analysis.
issues.evidence: 'This is the odd-prime case of the trichotomy in [uchida1981, §1, pp. 595–596], together with its Proposition 1... The open-image hypothesis, rather than surjectivity onto P_N, suffices.' No argument is given for this sentence.

coverage: I read all sections (1308 lines of LaTeX) and checked every step of the internal argument. (1) Log-rank lemma: the Cauchy–Binet smallness bound η^{cA^{1+1/r}}, the Taylor coefficient bound, the translate/zero estimate (pigeonhole on dimensions, distinct translates via Zariski density, the Bezout component count (nD)^n against (S+1)^m), the archimedean bound, the product formula, and the exponent comparison n/r ≥ n/(n−1) > 1+n/m, which holds exactly when m > n(n−1). (2) Frobenius detection (i)–(iii): the class-field description of characters, the disjoint-support multiplicative independence argument, averaging, corestriction. (3) Signed representation: the multiplicity argument and faithfulness. (4) Normalizer extension and the nontriviality of the H_i. (5) Quotient amplification: rank of g−1 on F_2[R_1]^m, size of the conjugacy class, the character values of Ind sign, the bound dim W^D − dim W^C ≥ |R|(1/4n − η), and the choice of m. (6) Frobenius generation: residue degree f = [⟨δ⟩ : ⟨δ⟩∩H], T-equivariance of pullback, the decomposition into the f|j and f∤j parts, and the U-equivariant projection back to Y^{N_i} = j(X^{H_i}). (7) Surjectivity, and f=1 from ℓ ≡ 1 mod [k:Q]! together with the norm identity. (8) Finite fibers via the sign character and cor ≠ 0. (9) Uniform missed-prime bound: inflation injectivity, the ε^{-1}-eigenspace, the proof that the classes are unramified away from ℓ, and the orbit count ≤ 2[K:Q]. (10) Power-residue Chebotarev construction. (11) Matching residue characteristics. (12) Identification: (a_q)_r = 1 from the fixed-r log identity, equal pullbacks, faithfulness, the compactness argument, the centralizer step, and the final reduction to Hoshi. I found no gap in any of these.
